points.title: Cracking and unauthorised access
points.must: Cracking = gaining unauthorised access to a system or data, usually with malicious intent; unauthorised access = using it without the owner’s permission, even without changing anything.

points.title: Vulnerability
points.must: A weakness (unpatched bug, weak password, poor procedure) that an attacker can exploit.

points.title: Types of hacker
points.must: Black-hat (illegal, for gain or harm), white-hat (with permission, penetration testing), grey-hat (no permission, no criminal intent — still illegal).

points.title: Cracking methods
points.must: At least five: brute force, dictionary, phishing / social engineering, exploiting vulnerabilities, SQL injection, interception, keylogger — each with how it works.

points.title: Method and countermeasure
points.must: For each method the measure that stops it (e.g. brute force → lockout + strong passwords; interception → HTTPS); SQL injection example with input validation.

points.title: Ethical vs legal problems
points.must: Ethical = morally wrong (privacy, harm, trust); legal = breaks the law (Criminal Code, Law on Personal Data); one example of each.

points.title: Problems for individuals, organisations, society
points.must: Identity theft, privacy, money; financial loss, data theft, reputation, downtime; loss of trust, critical infrastructure.

points.title: Analysing an ethical problem
points.must: Chain: what happened → who is harmed → how → why it is wrong; a worked case (hospital or school marks website, responsible disclosure).

points.title: Authentication
points.must: Checking who the user is: something you know / have / are; 2FA needs two of them so a stolen password is not enough.

points.title: Authorisation and least privilege
points.must: Deciding what an authenticated user may do; access rights such as read-only for pupils, edit for teachers.

points.title: Encryption and hashing
points.must: Encryption is two-way with a key (data in transit — HTTPS, stored data); hashing is one-way, used to store passwords.

points.title: Other measures
points.must: Limit login attempts, firewall, updates / patches, logs and audit trails, blocking locations, training, physical security — each with how it protects.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: Authentication vs authorisation mixed up; encryption stops reading not stealing; firewall does not remove viruses.
